findings.title: CreamFinance
findings.description: Price Manipulation

findings.title: Unitroller.fallback() uses delegatecall to a input-controlled function id
findings.description:
The function delegatecalls into code chosen by the caller, so a stranger can run their code with this contract's storage and balance. Slither: Unitroller.fallback() (contracts/Unitroller.sol#135-147) uses delegatecall to a input-controlled function id
	- (success,None) = comptrollerImplementation.delegatecall(msg.data) (contracts/Unitroller.sol#137)

findings.title: CarefulMath.mulUInt(uint256,uint256) uses a dangerous strict equality
findings.description:
A strict equality on a balance or amount can be broken by someone sending a little extra, locking the logic. Slither: CarefulMath.mulUInt(uint256,uint256) (contracts/CarefulMath.sol#24-36) uses a dangerous strict equality:
	- a == 0 (contracts/CarefulMath.sol#25)

findings.title: Reentrancy in CToken.redeemFresh(address,uint256,uint256)
findings.description:
The function calls out to another contract before it finishes updating its own state. A malicious callee can re-enter while the state is half-written; no ether moves in the reentrant path itself, but the stale state can be abused. Slither: Reentrancy in CToken.redeemFresh(address,uint256,uint256) (contracts/CToken.sol#613-707):
	External calls:
	- allowed = comptroller.redeemAllowed(address(this),redeemer,vars.redeemTokens) (contracts/CToken.sol#653)
	State variables written after the call(s):
	- totalSupply = vars.totalSupplyNew (contracts/CToken.sol#696)
	CTokenStorage.totalSupply (contracts/CTokenInterfaces.sol#91) can be used in cross function reentrancies:
	- CToken.exchangeRateStoredInternal() (contracts/CToken.sol#339-369)
	- CTokenStorage.totalSupply (contracts/CTokenInterfaces.sol#91)
